issues.description: The script sends requests to third-party APIs (SponsorBlock and Cobalt instances) to fetch skip segments and video download links. These requests include the current YouTube video ID, which may be considered user activity data.
issues.location: CFG.sbApi, CFG.cobaltInstances, code sections using GM_xmlhttpRequest/fetch to these endpoints
issues.recommendation: Clearly inform users about the data sent to third-party APIs. Limit data to only what is necessary (e.g., video ID, not full URL or user info).

issues.description: The script uses GM_setValue and GM_getValue to store user toggle settings (ad skip, SponsorBlock, quality). While this is local, it is persistent and could be privacy-relevant if misused.
issues.location: Persistent state section (S object, save function)
issues.recommendation: Ensure only non-sensitive toggle states are stored. Do not store personal or sensitive data.

issues.description: The script requests GM_xmlhttpRequest permission and @connect to multiple third-party domains. This increases the attack surface if those endpoints are compromised.
issues.recommendation: Restrict @connect to only necessary domains. Monitor the security of third-party APIs.

details: Stores toggle states (ad skip, SponsorBlock, quality) in local storage via GM_setValue/GM_getValue

script_name: EasyTube V3 — Ad Skip, SponsorBlock & HD Download⬇️🚀
summary: The script is generally well-structured and does not use obfuscation, eval, or dynamic code execution. It does not collect sensitive user data or listen to keyboard/clipboard events. However, it does transmit YouTube video IDs to third-party APIs (SponsorBlock and Cobalt instances) to provide its core features, which is a privacy consideration. No DOM XSS or injection risks were found. The supply chain risk is moderate due to reliance on external APIs. Overall, the script is safe for most users, but those with strict privacy requirements should be aware of the data sent to third parties.
